recipe.label: Stained Glass

traits.medium: luminous stained-glass-looking cloud artwork built from translucent jewel-colored panes
traits.texture: subtle rippled glass surfaces, dark leading and light passing through colored panes
traits.composition: pane shapes follow the original cloud lobes and broad sky; avoid random decorative symbols
traits.lighting: backlit cream cloud panes against deep blue sky panes

review_checks: cloud silhouette organizes the pane layout
limitations: No fabrication pattern, cut lines or structurally validated glazing design is supplied.
Palette and fine geometry are prompt guidance and require visual review across a series.

assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: README style reference; intended use: One reviewed Stained Glass example for the Art Skill style catalog
Primary request: A towering white cumulus cloud with bright sunlit upper-right lobes and cool shadowed lower-left volumes, rising into a large deep-blue sky. Tiny dark foliage and roofline details sit only along the bottom edge.
Style/medium: luminous stained-glass-looking cloud artwork built from translucent jewel-colored panes
Color palette: #183C71, #427BA8, #B9DCDD, #F1E4BE, #292B38
Materials/textures: subtle rippled glass surfaces, dark leading and light passing through colored panes
Composition/framing: pane shapes follow the original cloud lobes and broad sky; avoid random decorative symbols; Keep portrait orientation and the original broad framing; one image, no frame or panels
Lighting/mood: backlit cream cloud panes against deep blue sky panes
Requested output target: 1024x1536, opaque background, png; use only supported tool controls
Avoid: real people; copyrighted characters; logos and brand marks; copied artworks; unrequested lettering
Constraints: Keep the original upward sky viewpoint, large lobed cloud shape, light/shadow arrangement and broad upper sky. Foreground remains a small lower-edge suggestion. Do not add a sea, island bay, garden, sunset or rainbow.; No added people, brands, characters, captions or signatures; Use only this source photograph as the composition reference; never mix motifs from the other photos
